en: edited by Mahāmahopādhyāya Hara Prasad Shastri.
In the *Advayavajrasaṃgraha*, edited by the Mikkyō Seiten Kenkyūkai and published as GOS 1927 in Baroda;
and in the *Taishō Daigaku Sōgō Bukkyō Kenkyūjo Nenpō*.
The appearance, which is excellent and lovely, is merely dependent origination.
It would not exist if emptiness were considered to be like a dead woman or a mere phantom. (1)
She who is the beloved of emptiness, supreme and incomparable in form—if she were ever separate [from him], the beloved leader would be consumed by fire. (2)
(82/283) Therefore, the couple approached the Guru with apprehension;
by means of his own affection for them, he caused their innate love to be manifested. || 3 ||
O Vāyu, such is the great scholarship and supreme skill of the True Guru;
both have become unsurpassed, free from support and non-different from their own nature. (4)
Complete with all the marks, free from the two extremes, the intrinsic nature of all phenomena, yet devoid of self-nature, they are ever-arisen. (5)
